narrative:
The model estimates an 84% chance that you will leave your job. Because that is a high retention risk, the organization has decided not to promote you at this time, based on the prediction that you are likely to depart soon.

The strongest signal driving this prediction is that you have received other job opportunities while working here. Among employees predicted to stay, about 77% had no such outside offers, so your situation stands out as a clear flight risk. Your total years of experience also push toward leaving: at 6–10 years, you are more experienced than the typical stayer, half of whom had only 1–5 years, which may make you more attractive to other employers. Finally, working in the 'other' sector adds to the leaving prediction, since stayers are more often found in medical or education sectors.

These three factors all point in the same direction: the model sees you as likely to move on. Therefore, a promotion now may not retain you. The organization should discuss your career intentions and external options with you, and consider whether a promotion, new challenges, or other incentives could change your decision. You should reflect on whether you want to stay and what would make you commit.
